title: Does Size Buy Trust?
description: An independent review of visible trust evidence across three Canadian apparel brands.

sections.heading: Evidence needs to reach the product page
sections.body: The report found useful brand evidence on About pages that was not consistently visible on the sampled product pages. A shopper may need that evidence closer to the decision.

sections.heading: Make the scoring method visible
sections.body: Each of sixteen author-defined criteria was marked present, partial or absent on the sampled material. The framework is a structured review aid; it is not a Google E-E-A-T score.

sections.heading: Use the gaps to ask better questions
sections.body: For a follow-up audit, I would check whether important product and brand claims have accessible support, who is responsible for them, and whether the evidence is visible in the purchase journey.

methodology: Five pages each from A Bronze Age, tentree and Herschel were reviewed on 24 October 2026. Sixteen criteria were grouped under experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust, with scores of 1, 0.5 or 0.
limitations: Three brands cannot establish whether business size causes trust or search performance. Not observed on a sampled page does not mean absent sitewide. Page sampling and collapsed content affect what the review can detect.
